items.front: Which solution will meet these requirements ___ly?
items.extra: the cheapest option that still meets every requirement first reject every option that fails a requirement, then pick the cheapest of the rest

items.front: Which solution will meet these requirements with the ___?
items.extra: the team does the least work to run it a managed or serverless feature, not scripts or software on instances

items.front: Which solution will provide access in the ___ way?
items.extra: the strongest protection among options that work least privilege, temporary credentials and private access, even when another option is cheaper

items.front: The company needs a ___ architecture for the web tier.
items.extra: it keeps working when one part fails; this book: a short interruption is acceptable more than one Availability Zone, a load balancer or automatic failover

items.front: The application must be ___ if one Availability Zone becomes unavailable.
items.extra: it keeps working when one part fails; this book: with no interruption stronger than highly available in this book: spare capacity is already running

items.front: Which design is the ___ to the failure of an Availability Zone?
items.extra: it recovers from failure best remove single points of failure and automate recovery

items.front: Users around the world need the ___ when they load the images.
items.extra: the shortest wait for a response move data or compute closer to the user: caching, edge services, the nearest Region

items.front: What is the ___ way to collect the logs?
items.extra: it meets the need with the least ongoing work and fewest moving parts a built-in feature of the service, not a custom solution

items.front: Which solution will meet these requirements with the ___?
items.extra: the developers write or change the least code a configuration change or a compatible managed service, not a redesign

items.front: The company needs a ___ solution that handles the growth in traffic.
items.extra: it can handle more load when the load grows automatic scaling or a service that scales without capacity planning

items.front: The application receives ___ requests during the day.
items.extra: sometimes, not regularly pay per use; not instances that run all the time

items.front: The reporting database has ___ usage and is idle most of the night.
items.extra: it starts and stops, with pauses between capacity that can pause or scale to zero; pay per use

items.front: Traffic to the new application is ___.
items.extra: you cannot plan the load automatic scaling, on-demand capacity, or a queue as a buffer

items.front: The order service has sudden spikes in traffic during sales events.
items.extra: the load jumps up quickly for a short time a buffer in front of slow parts, and scaling that reacts fast

items.front: The production instances have ___ usage all year.
items.extra: the same load all the time a commitment discount or provisioned capacity

items.front: The batch job runs on a ___ schedule every night.
items.extra: you know the load in advance scheduled scaling or a commitment; no need for the most flexible option

items.front: Each ___ job processes one large video file.
items.extra: one job runs for a long time check the maximum run time of the compute option; containers or instances fit long jobs

items.front: The ___ tasks start when a file arrives.
items.extra: each job finishes quickly functions that start on an event

items.front: The ___ web tier runs on instances behind a load balancer.
items.extra: the application keeps no memory between requests any instance can serve any request, so instances can be added, removed or interrupted

items.front: The image-processing jobs ___ and can be restarted.
items.extra: stopping the work and starting it again is acceptable spare capacity at a discount that AWS can take back

items.front: All data ___ be encrypted before the data leaves the application.
items.extra: it is a hard requirement an option that does not meet it is wrong, even if the option is cheaper or easier

items.front: The company has ___ compliance requirements for audit logs.
items.extra: very demanding the strongest control, not the cheapest

items.front: A security policy ___ that no instance has a public IP address.
items.extra: a rule from outside the team requires it treat it as a hard constraint, and prefer a control that enforces it centrally

items.front: The architect must ___ that objects cannot be deleted for one year.
items.extra: make it certain a hard requirement; if an action must not happen, prevent it, not only alert

items.front: The company runs a ___ order database.
items.extra: the business stops if it fails pay for availability and fast recovery; the cheapest design is probably wrong

items.front: A delay of several hours to retrieve the files is ___.
items.extra: the business allows it a relaxed requirement: a cheaper or simpler option is now allowed

items.front: The company must keep the logs for at least 7 years.
items.extra: this much or more a lower limit: check that capacity or retention never falls below it

items.front: The company ___ managing any servers.
items.extra: the company does not accept this remove every option that includes the unwanted thing

items.front: A recovery time of several hours is ___ for the test environment.
items.extra: enough for the need do not choose more than is needed; the larger option costs more

items.front: The company must move the data to AWS ___.
items.extra: with the shortest delay the fastest option that meets the other constraints; watch the transfer or retrieval time

items.front: The dashboard must show the sensor readings in real time.
items.extra: with no noticeable delay the smallest delay; a reading rule of this book, compare with near real-time

items.front: The clickstream data must be available for analysis in ___.
items.extra: a short delay is acceptable a short delay is allowed, so a service that buffers data can fit

items.front: After 30 days, the documents are ___.
items.extra: people read the data only sometimes a cheaper storage class; check the retrieval charge and how fast a read must be

items.front: Regulations require that the records are ___ for 5 years.
items.extra: nobody can change or delete the data a lock that prevents changes, not only versioning

items.front: The company must ___ the backups for 90 days.
items.extra: keep the data for a set time lifecycle rules and retention settings; count the required period

items.front: The company wants to ___ the audio files for 7 years.
items.extra: store data for a long time and read it almost never the coldest storage that still meets the retrieval time in the stem

items.front: The uploaded files must be stored in a highly ___ way.
items.extra: the data is not lost storage that keeps copies in several places; durability is not the same as availability

items.front: The team must restore the database to a ___ before the error.
items.extra: the state of the data at one exact moment continuous backups or snapshots; check how far back and how exact

items.front: The replicas are ___ consistent with the primary.
items.extra: after some time, not maybe a short delay before all readers see a change is acceptable

items.front: The application runs ___ queries with joins across many tables.
items.extra: several changes succeed together or fail together a database with ACID transactions: a relational engine, or Amazon DynamoDB transactions

items.front: The company wants a ___ message broker.
items.extra: AWS does the operating work choose the AWS service over the same software installed on instances

items.front: The company wants a ___ solution for the new API.
items.extra: no servers for the team to manage or size functions, managed containers without instances, and on-demand data services

items.front: The team does not want to ___ capacity for peak load.
items.extra: create and size a resource in advance provisioned means capacity you choose and pay for; the opposite is on-demand

items.front: The operations team spends too much time on ___ing the database servers.
items.extra: install software fixes work the team wants to give away: a managed service, or an automated patch tool

items.front: The company wants to ___ the rotation of database credentials.
items.extra: make it happen without a person a built-in schedule, rule or policy, not a manual runbook

items.front: A solutions architect must ___ the web tier from the processing tier.
items.extra: separate two parts so one keeps working when the other is slow or fails a queue, a topic or an event bus between the parts

items.front: The company needs to ___ a multi-step order workflow.
items.extra: run several steps in order, with retries and decisions a workflow service, not code that calls each step by hand

items.front: The security team wants to ___ firewall rules across all accounts.
items.extra: control many accounts or resources from one place an organization-wide service or policy, not a setting repeated in each account

items.front: The team wants to ___ CPU usage and be notified of high values.
items.extra: watch and be told when something happens metrics and alarms for performance; an audit trail for who did what

items.front: The startup has ___ with no experience in running Kubernetes.
items.extra: few people run the system the same as least operational overhead: prefer managed services

items.front: The solution must follow the principle of ___.
items.extra: only the permissions that the task needs a narrow policy on a role; never broad permissions or shared credentials

items.front: All data must be encrypted ___.
items.extra: while the data is stored storage encryption with a key service; check who must control the key

items.front: The company must encrypt the data ___ between the application and the database.
items.extra: while the data moves over a network TLS and certificates; check whether requests that are not encrypted must be refused

items.front: The database password must be ___d every 30 days.
items.extra: replace a key or a password with a new one on a schedule a secrets service with built-in rotation, not a script

items.front: An ___or must see who deleted the security group.
items.extra: keep a record of who did what and when the API activity trail and the configuration history, not performance metrics

items.front: The company must ___ access to the bucket to one VPC.
items.extra: allow only some people or networks a policy condition, a resource-based policy or a network rule that names what is allowed

items.front: The bucket stores ___ customer documents.
items.extra: data that causes harm if other people see it encryption, tight access, and a service that discovers such data

items.front: The company must ___ the production workload from development.
items.extra: keep apart so that one cannot reach the other separate accounts, VPCs, subnets or security groups, by how strong the isolation must be

items.front: External auditors need ___ access to the reports.
items.extra: it stops working after a set time roles and temporary credentials, or a time-limited link; never long-term keys

items.front: The company must manage its own encryption keys and control their rotation.
items.extra: the company, not AWS, controls the encryption keys customer managed keys in a key service; check who must control rotation

items.front: The company runs an application ___ and wants to back up the data to AWS.
items.extra: in the company's own data center, not in AWS a hybrid question: think about the network link, the transfer tool and where identities live

items.front: The company needs a ___ storage solution for its file servers.
items.extra: AWS and the data center work together private connectivity, and services that extend AWS storage or identity to the data center

items.front: The instances must access the service ___, without traversing the internet.
items.extra: the traffic stays off the public internet VPC endpoints inside AWS; a dedicated or private link from outside

items.front: The company hosts an ___ web application.
items.extra: users on the internet reach it directly a public entry point with protection in front; the tiers behind it stay private

items.front: ___ report slow downloads of static content.
items.extra: users are far from one Region edge caching, global routing or more than one Region

items.front: The instances run ___.
items.extra: copies or capacity in more than one zone of one Region protection against a zone failure; not protection against a Region failure

items.front: The company requires ___ disaster recovery for the database.
items.extra: between two Regions disaster recovery or global users; replication features and their cost

items.front: The company needs a ___ with consistent network performance.
items.extra: a private network line that only this company uses a dedicated physical link, compared with a VPN that runs over the internet

items.front: The company wants to block malicious requests at the ___.
items.extra: at AWS sites near the users content delivery and protection before traffic reaches the Region

items.front: Because of ___ rules, the data must remain in one Region.
items.extra: the law says where the data is stored keep data and backups in the named Region; reject options that copy data elsewhere

items.front: A company plans to ___ 60 TB of data to Amazon S3.
items.extra: move an application or data to AWS find the size, the time limit and the network link; they decide the tool

items.front: The company wants to ___ the application to AWS.
items.extra: move the application without changing it instances and a rehosting tool, not a new serverless design

items.front: The company needs higher availability ___.
items.extra: keep the code as it is a compatible managed service or a change in configuration, not a redesign

items.front: The solution must require ___.
items.extra: small code changes are acceptable a service with a compatible interface; reject a full rewrite

items.front: The company is willing to ___ the application to reduce cost.
items.extra: change the design of the application the stem allows new services such as functions, queues or containers

items.front: A ___ application uses a standard messaging protocol.
items.extra: an old system that is hard to change keep its protocols and interfaces; prefer services that support them

items.front: The company runs a ___ application on one large instance.
items.extra: one large application where all parts depend on each other a question about splitting it or decoupling its parts

items.front: The database migration must have ___.
items.extra: the system stops for a very short time or not at all replication before the switch, not a backup and restore

items.front: The company needs ___ from the source database until the cutover.
items.extra: changes keep flowing from the source to the target a replication or change-data-capture feature, not a one-time copy

items.front: The company needs a ___ transfer of archived video files.
items.extra: it happens once no need for a permanent link or service; compare transfer time with a shipped device

items.back: Which solution will meet these requirements?
items.extra: choose the one option that satisfies every requirement in the stem list the requirements first; an option that misses one requirement is wrong

items.front: What should a solutions architect do to meet ___?
items.extra: all the needs stated before the question go back and count them; there are often two or three

items.front: Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? ___
items.extra: exactly that number of options are correct judge each option as true or false on its own, then count that you marked the right number

items.front: ___ should a solutions architect take?
items.extra: the correct options work together as one solution the chosen options must not conflict; often one is the service and one is its configuration

items.front: Which solution is the MOST cost-effective?
items.extra: often more than one option works; rank the options that work the capital word names the ranking rule; find it before reading the options

items.front: Which storage solution ___ meets these requirements?
items.extra: the option that fits the stated requirements most completely several options are possible; the stem's constraints decide, not your preference

items.front: The company ___ stores the files on an EC2 instance.
items.extra: how the system is now the starting point; the answer changes as little of it as the requirements allow

items.front: The company ___ reduce the load on the primary database.
items.extra: the goal of the company the sentence with this phrase usually holds the requirement

items.front: A solutions architect ___ design a solution that scales automatically.
items.extra: a requirement, as strong as must treat it as a hard constraint

items.front: ___, users report errors during peak hours.
items.extra: a problem or a change follows the sentence after it describes what is wrong; the answer fixes that one thing
